interpretations: Group joined standings rows by `races.name` across all years. For each name, count all standings rows and average its non-null `driverStandings.points`. Keep names whose row count exceeds the unweighted mean row count across names. Return the unweighted mean of the kept names’ point averages, the mean of their row counts, and that mean row count minus the overall mean row count.
Use the same calculation, but count only standings rows with non-null `driverStandings.points` when measuring field size.
Use the same calculation, but measure each race name’s field size by its number of distinct drivers across all occurrences.

For each race occurrence, count its standings rows and average its non-null points. For each race name, use the mean of those occurrence-level field sizes and the mean of those occurrence-level point averages; then apply the stated filter and final averages across names.
Use the per-name calculations in interpretation 1, but compare each name’s field size with the average field size of individual race occurrences, rather than the average of the per-name field sizes.

Use the per-name calculations and filter in interpretation 1, but report the average percentage by which the selected names’ field sizes exceed the overall average, rather than their average absolute excess.
Use the per-race-occurrence calculation, but count only standings rows with non-null points when measuring each occurrence’s field size.
Use the per-race-occurrence calculation, but count distinct drivers in each occurrence when measuring its field size.
queries:
WITH name_stats AS (
  SELECT r.name,
         COUNT(*) AS row_count,
         AVG(ds.points) AS point_avg
  FROM driverStandings AS ds
  JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(row_count) AS mean_row_count
  FROM name_stats
)
SELECT AVG(ns.point_avg),
       AVG(ns.row_count),
       AVG(ns.row_count) - o.mean_row_count
FROM name_stats AS ns
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE ns.row_count > o.mean_row_count
